title: Work as prayer
hookLine: Colossians 3:23: whatever you do, do it heartily as to the Lord
tomorrow: what did a blind man shout that the crowd tried to hush?

cards: A sink full of dishes. A shift that starts before sunrise. A spreadsheet at nine.
A big share of a day can go to work, paid or unpaid, and it rarely feels like the holy part. A letter to a small church in Colossae says the dishes count. It doesn't tell anyone to stop and go pray.
It tells them how to do the work in front of them.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.” Whatsoever: no list of holy jobs and ordinary ones.
Heartily: the whole self, not just the hands. As to the Lord: the boss and the customer are still there, but the work is handed to someone else too.

Notice who first heard it. The verses just before speak to servants, people whose work wasn't chosen and often wasn't fair. The verse doesn't make that hardship fine, and readers still wrestle with it.
What it does claim is that no work is too small to offer. Now look back at the week. It began with a book left on a table and a chain of readers.
Then the first thought of the morning, given to God. The whole day handed over, in set words or your own. Three stops: morning, noon and night.
A pause at the table. And today, the long middle of the day: the work. Each piece is small.
Together they're starting to look like a day.

how: Some Christians offer their work to God at the start of the day or the start of a task, and some keep a short line like Colossians 3:23 near the place they work.

o: the work itself, done heartily, offered to God
a prayer said together before a shift starts
being paid to lead prayers in a church

games.q: your summer job is folding shirts nobody will ever thank you for. what does Colossians 3:23 suggest?
o: fold fast, and save your real prayers for after the shift.
quit for a job that feels more meaningful and holy.
fold them heartily, as to the Lord, not only for the manager.
games.why: whatsoever ye do: there's no list of holy jobs. the folding itself can be the offering.

practice: Pick one small job within reach: a cup to rinse, a desk to clear, a bed to straighten. Do it slowly and well, as if it were being handed to someone who matters, and stop when it's done.
If you pray, offer it with the letter's words: as to the Lord.

wordCard.voice: Work as prayer. The work itself offered to God, done heartily, not prayers stacked on top of it.

orig.note: the Greek behind heartily in Colossians 3:23, word for word: from the soul.

carryVoice: Carry this: heartily, as to the Lord, even at the sink. A week of small pieces, done.
